headline: Over 724,000 students vanished from the education ladder before HSC exams
summary: Official figures reveal a massive dropout rate between SSC and HSC, with the technical stream hit hardest by a 54.58% decline.
details: Over 724,000 students who passed the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination two years ago are no longer on the path to completing higher secondary education.
Of the 1.67 million students who passed the SSC in 2024, 180,221 never even enrolled in college, while 543,989 who did enroll failed to submit examination forms for this year's HSC tests.
The Technical Education Board saw the steepest decline, with 54.58% of its cohort—90,345 students—absent from this year's examinations.
General education boards lost 33.04% of their students, while the Madrasah Education Board saw a 44.07% dropout rate among Alim programme students.
Experts, including Prof Md Azam Khan of Jagannath University, attribute this crisis to severe unemployment, financial hardship, and social pressures such as child marriage.
Many students are reportedly entering the labour market immediately after SSC due to a loss of faith in the academic value of degrees, as even university graduates struggle to find jobs.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has stated that the government needs to find answers as to why students are dropping out at such an alarming rate.
Officials suggest that while some may have permanently abandoned education, others might have delayed enrollment due to temporary financial difficulties.
caption:
724,000 students gone. A generation is slipping through the cracks of Bangladesh's education system.

Over 724,000 students who passed the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination two years ago are no longer on the path to completing higher secondary education.

Of the 1.67 million students who passed the SSC in 2024, 180,221 never even enrolled in college, while 543,989 who did enroll failed to submit examination forms for this year's HSC tests.

The Technical Education Board saw the steepest decline, with 54.58% of its cohort—90,345 students—absent from this year's examinations.

General education boards lost 33.04% of their students, while the Madrasah Education Board saw a 44.07% dropout rate among Alim programme students.

Experts, including Prof Md Azam Khan of Jagannath University, attribute this crisis to severe unemployment, financial hardship, and social pressures such as child marriage.

Many students are reportedly entering the labour market immediately after SSC due to a loss of faith in the academic value of degrees, as even university graduates struggle to find jobs.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has stated that the government needs to find answers as to why students are dropping out at such an alarming rate.

Officials suggest that while some may have permanently abandoned education, others might have delayed enrollment due to temporary financial difficulties.

headline_marked: 1% minimum fee: [[Merchants to pay for Bangla QR transactions]]
headline: 1% minimum fee: Merchants to pay for Bangla QR transactions
summary: Bangladesh Bank has introduced a minimum Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for digital payments via the Bangla QR system.
details: Bangladesh Bank has set a minimum fee of 1 percent, including VAT, that banks and payment providers can charge merchants for transactions made through the Bangla QR system.
The order takes effect immediately, according to a central bank circular issued today.

This fee, known as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), applies to payments made via bank accounts, debit and prepaid cards, credit cards, mobile financial services (MFS), or Payment Service Provider (PSP) channels.
The rule applies as long as the transaction uses Bangla QR under the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB).
The latest circular replaces parts of a February 6 order that previously set MDR ceilings for Point of Sale (POS), Bangla QR, and e-commerce transactions.
Other fee limits and conditions from the February circular remain unchanged; only the new minimum fee now applies.
Banks or PSPs may still run promotional campaigns to encourage digital transactions, allowing them to offer rates below the new floor during such periods.
caption:
Digital payments are getting a new cost for merchants. Bangladesh Bank now mandates a minimum 1% fee for Bangla QR transactions.

Bangladesh Bank has set a minimum fee of 1 percent, including VAT, that banks and payment providers can charge merchants for transactions made through the Bangla QR system.

The order takes effect immediately, according to a central bank circular issued today.

This fee, known as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), applies to payments made via bank accounts, debit and prepaid cards, credit cards, mobile financial services (MFS), or Payment Service Provider (PSP) channels.

The rule applies as long as the transaction uses Bangla QR under the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB).

The latest circular replaces parts of a February 6 order that previously set MDR ceilings for Point of Sale (POS), Bangla QR, and e-commerce transactions.

Other fee limits and conditions from the February circular remain unchanged; only the new minimum fee now applies.

Banks or PSPs may still run promotional campaigns to encourage digital transactions, allowing them to offer rates below the new floor during such periods.
